Jonas / team — reviewed BlueHarbor's redline and K&E's note. High-level counsel position below; suggested text inlined in the attached matrix (Subprocessor_Matrix_BH.xlsx).

Key points / proposed positions:
- Bridging language: we can accept a limited bridging clause that references the then-current SCCs and commits both parties to adopt approved transfer mechanisms. Proposed language: "Where applicable, the parties shall rely on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses or other lawful transfer mechanisms; if such mechanisms are not available, the parties will implement reasonable supplementary measures and cooperate in good faith to enable lawful transfers." This avoids creating an open-ended undertaking.
- Subprocessor notice/objection: agree to prior notice but push back on 15 business days for objection. Counter: 10 business days for objection, with an escalation path (technical call) for critical subprocessors.
- Audit rights: restrict to a single annual on-site or remote audit unless there's a material incident; require an NDA prior to any audit report sharing.
- Retention table: ask BH to map their retention needs to specific product data categories; we can accept customer-specific retention only where documented in SOW.
- Liability cap clarification: confirm that transfer mechanisms do not increase our liability beyond the negotiated cap.

Action items:
1) I will produce a redline with suggested bracketed language for the bridging clause (ETA: EOD Friday).
2) Marissa — please prepare DocuSign routing recommendations once we agree language.
3) Priyom — if they insist on 15-day objection, we'll need to quantify the commercial concession we expect (e.g., extended term commitment or modest discount).
